subject: Embeddings fit validation follow-up / next steps

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-18T15:02:00Z
Subject: Embeddings fit validation follow-up / next steps

Hi Elena 

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned: 

- Recap: You shared that Acme Search is evaluating a semantic ranking replacement for an internal search product (approx 1M documents, mostly product content + vendor docs). Key constraints: tight latency (p95 < 120ms), ability to detect semantic drift over time, and keeping embedding size reasonable to manage ANN costs.
- What we'll deliver this week: 1) a short eval of recommended candidate embedding models run on your sample set (we'll provide nearest-neighbor recall and MRR), 2) a baseline dimensionality/size recommendation and cost estimate, 3) a short prompt set / query set you can use for regression checks.

Next steps:
1) I attached the sample set and initial eval template you mentioned — please confirm this is representative (attached: acme-embeddings-sample-set.csv).
2) Rishi will run model-fit experiments (3 candidate models + quantized variants) and share metrics and example failure cases by Thursday.
3) Marissa will coordinate a 30-minute follow-up next week to review results and agree on a pilot SLA.

If that all looks right, I'll schedule the follow-up for Tues/Wed next week. Also calling out 2 risks we flagged on the call:
- Potential quality regression when moving from a dense model to a quantized variant for latency/cost reasons
- Drift detection requires an evaluation harness and baseline query set — I included a proposed small regression prompt set in the Drive link.

Thanks again — looking forward to the eval.

Best,
Marcus
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
D: +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: acme-embeddings-sample-set.csv (CSV, 12k rows)

Thanks Marcus 

this is great, and the recap matches our notes. A couple quick clarifications before you run the experiments: 

- The sample set is representative but we have a heavier tail of vendor docs (longer text fields). I marked those rows in the CSV with "long_doc" in the notes column.
- Latency SLO: the 120ms p95 is for the entire request path (embedding compute + ANN lookup). We estimate network + lookup to be ~40ms on our infra, so embedding inference should aim for ~80ms p95.

Also attaching a quick export of our current evaluation labels (acme-eval-results-20260817.csv) — it contains binary relevance judgments across 5,000 queries. Two asks:
1) Can you include semantic search metrics (NDCG@10, MRR, recall@100) in the eval?
2) Please surface examples where model similarity scores disagree with human labels — those will help us understand failure modes.

On scheduling: Tue/Wed both work — Raj would like to join the follow-up to talk about operational constraints.

Elena
Head of Search 
Acme Search

Subject: Re: Embeddings fit validation follow-up / next steps

Hi Elena 

thanks for the quick turnaround and for the labeled export. A few notes on the experiment plan and what we'll include in the delivery: 

Experiment plan (running now):
- Candidate models: redwood-embed-1024 (dense), open-embed-768 (open), redwood-embed-512-quant (quantized 8-bit)
- Metrics: NDCG@10, MRR, recall@100, cosine similarity distribution, and per-query disagreement with human labels.
- Dimensionality: we'll test 512 vs 768 vs 1024, and report ANN memory estimates (RAM/SSD) for different ANN indexes (HNSW, DiskANN) at your target recall.
- Drift check: we'll run a simple time-based split (older vs newer docs) on your sample to surface semantic drift and per-query stability.

Preliminary findings (short):
- On a 1k-subset quick run: redwood-embed-1024 gives best NDCG@10 and MRR. open-embed-768 is close on average but has more variance on vendor docs (longer docs). The quantized 512 variant reduces vector size by ~50% and inference latency by ~30% but shows a 6-8% drop in NDCG on the labeled set.

Deliverables by Thursday (full CSV + a short writeup):
- Per-model metric CSV with top-k retrieval and aggregated metrics (we'll attach acme-eval-results-20260819-redwood.csv)
- Short list of top 10 failure example queries with candidate passages and model scores
- Recommendation: if you need highest quality, prefer redwood-embed-1024; if ANN cost/latency dominates, consider redwood-embed-512-quant but only with a regression guard and monthly eval checks.

I'll attach the full result files to the follow-up email. For the meeting, Tue/Wed next week works — I'm flexible on time.

— Rishi
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
